title: Every Step of the Way: Video-based Parkinsonian Turning Step Counting
abstract: arXiv:2606.27918v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As a prominent symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), turning impairment is evaluated through parameters such as turning angle, duration, and particularly, the number of steps required to complete a turn, which directly reflects motor dysfunction. Accurate step counting is challenging due to variability in real-world turning movements and atypical shuffling patterns in parkinsonian gait. Existing methods are predominantly wearable-based, requiring users to wear and manage dedicated devices, which can be inconvenient for continuous daily use. To address this, we propose a passive, video-based framework that estimates step count in a coarse-to-fine manner using diverse motion representations. Specifically, an initial step count is estimated from foot movement signals derived from 3D human mesh recovery, providing high-level motion structures. translated_title: 每一步：基于视频的帕金森病转身步数计数
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.27918v2 公告类型：替换-交叉  摘要：作为帕金森病（PD）的一个显著症状，转身障碍通过转身角度、持续时间，尤其是完成转身所需的步数等参数进行评估，这直接反映了运动功能障碍。由于现实世界中转身动作的变异性和帕金森步态中非典型的拖步模式，准确步数计数具有挑战性。现有方法主要基于可穿戴设备，要求用户佩戴和管理专用装置，这对于日常持续使用可能不便。为解决此问题，我们提出了一种被动的、基于视频的框架，利用多样运动表征以由粗到细的方式估计步数。具体而言，初始步数从3D人体网格恢复中提取的足部运动信号估算，提供高层运动结构。为融入细粒度运动细节，运动编码器学习互补的步态动态。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于视频的被动式帕金森病转身步数计数框架，采用由粗到细策略结合3D人体网格和运动编码器，克服了可穿戴设备不便和真实世界动作变异性问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a passive video-based framework for counting Parkinsonian turning steps, using a coarse-to-fine strategy combining 3D human mesh and motion encoder to overcome wearable device inconvenience and real-world movement variability.
